result.title: Off-the-Shelf Autonomous Agents for Game Playtesting
result.summary: In playtesting games, a human operator is typically required to test most gameplay elements. In this work we present Buddy, an autonomous game solving agent which can solve long time horizon objectives in an unseen 3D role-playing game using off-the-shelf language model systems. Buddy will take actions, receive feedback on those actions, and pursue a goal across many turns. No written walkthrough or model training of any kind is required, and we show that this paradigm holds in a novel environment where the agent must discover solutions via exploration rather than recalling them from pretraining. We demonstrate three downstream capabilities: game solving with no provided walkthrough, logging bug tickets for encountered difficulties, and conversion of successful agent traces into scripted hierarchical task networks for regression testing. Unlike existing playtesting solutions, our framework is fully modular: language models and harnesses can be easily swapped out as capabilities improve over time.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 Buddy，一个用现成语言模型驱动的游戏试玩智能体，在未见过的 3D 角色扮演游戏中通过多轮行动—反馈循环完成长时程目标，并把成功轨迹转为分层任务网络用于回归测试。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「靠探索而非预训练记忆发现解法」的多轮证据获取与行动决策循环，可能为 LVR 中 THINK/LOOK/STOP 的成本分配与停止判断提供外部参照，但属于应用级智能体框架，没有涉及内部视觉状态或 latent 表示，可供核查的借鉴较间接。
